channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: DemirBank Launches Online Sole Proprietor Registration via Mobile App
item.description: DemirBank has introduced a new digital service allowing clients to register as sole proprietors directly through its mobile application. This eliminates the need to visit tax authorities, streamlining the process from application to result within the DemirBank app.

item.title: New Corn Drying and Storage Complex Launched in Kazakhstan's Syrdariya Region
item.description: A new corn drying and storage complex has been launched by "Kyzylorda Starch-Syrup Plant" LLP in the Syrdariya district. This facility is expected to boost the region's agro-industrial sector and create hundreds of new jobs upon full completion. The initiative aligns with national goals for water resource management and agricultural product processing.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Farmers Prepare for Winter Livestock Challenges
item.description: Kazakhstan's agricultural sector is preparing for the winter season, with livestock numbers increasing. Local authorities report sufficient fodder reserves have been gathered. Farmers are working to ensure their herds are well-fed and healthy through the cold months.

item.title: Global Oil Prices Increase Amidst Middle East Tensions
item.description: Global oil prices saw a slight increase, with Brent crude futures trading around $92.50 per barrel and WTI futures near $82.93. This rise is attributed to reports of attacks in Saudi Arabia and incidents involving tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, following recent Iranian actions.

item.title: US Senate Passes Resolution Urging Trump to End War Against Iran
item.description: The US Senate approved a resolution calling on the government to cease military actions against Iran. Fifty senators voted in favor, with 48 against. While non-binding, the resolution expresses lawmakers' stance. The text urges President Trump to withdraw US forces from combat operations against the Islamic Republic of Iran.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prioritizes Energy Security as Key to Economic Independence
item.description: Kazakhstan is focusing on energy security to strengthen economic independence, with demand for electricity rising due to industrial and digital growth. The government aims to achieve surplus electricity production by 2029 through new power plant construction and grid modernization. Currently, coal power dominates the energy mix.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Atyrau Wagon Assembly Plant Begins Exporting Freight Wagons
item.description: The Atyrau wagon assembly plant in Kazakhstan has begun exporting its products after receiving EAEU certificates in December 2024. The factory, which is the first full-cycle freight wagon plant built from scratch in Central Asia, has a production capacity of 6,000-8,000 wagons per year. It produces various types of wagons, including semi-wagons, covered wagons, hopper wagons, and tank wagons.

item.title: Russian President Putin Arrives in Tajikistan for Working Visit
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Tajikistan for a working visit on Tuesday morning, coming from Shenzhen, China. He is scheduled to hold talks with Tajik leader Emomali Rahmon. Discussions will focus on security issues, trade and economic ties, major bilateral projects, and the further development of the strategic partnership between Russia and Tajikistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Older Workers Face Job Search Difficulties, Downshifting Common
item.description: Unemployment among Kazakh citizens aged over 50 is nearly double the national average. Approximately one in three job seekers in this age group encounters significant challenges finding employment, often leading to a career downgrade or reduced salary.

item.title: Kazakhstan Systematically Recovers Illegally Acquired Assets for Public Benefit
item.description: Kazakhstan is implementing a systematic policy to return illegally acquired assets, initiated by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. The goal is to restore social justice, strengthen the rule of law, and utilize national wealth for the benefit of the people. A dedicated company manages and sells these recovered assets through open auctions.

item.title: Turkmenistan urged to speed up gas pipeline construction to China via Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Parliament Speaker Marlen Mamataliev urged Turkmenistan to accelerate the construction of a major gas pipeline from Turkmenistan to China through Kyrgyzstan. The proposal was made during a meeting with Turkmenistan's Mejlis Speaker Dunyagozel Gulmanova. Cooperation in energy and transport logistics was also discussed.

item.title: Beeline owner VEON explores obtaining a banking license in Uzbekistan
item.description: VEON, the international telecommunications group and owner of Beeline Uzbekistan, is exploring the possibility of obtaining a banking license in Uzbekistan. The company is evaluating options to either acquire an existing bank or establish a new one. This move aligns with VEON's strategy to expand its financial services beyond mobile operations in Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kazakhstan to limit unemployment benefits to three months from 2027
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Kazakhstan will limit unemployment benefit payments to three months. The monthly payment will increase to 346,500 tenge, calculated as 45% of the average monthly income from social contributions over the past two years, capped at seven minimum wages. Eligibility will be restricted to participants of the mandatory social insurance system.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and France Hold Consultations on UN Security Council Agenda
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and France conducted consultations in Bishkek on the agenda of the UN Security Council. The parties discussed key aspects of the council's activities and exchanged views on current international issues in preparation for Kyrgyzstan's upcoming membership in the UNSC for 2027-2028. Both sides confirmed their readiness for further constructive cooperation within the organization.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks 16th in UN E-Government Development Index, Surpassing Japan and Germany
item.description: Kazakhstan has climbed to 16th place in the UN E-Government Development Index, entering the top tier for the first time. The country now ranks alongside Singapore, Denmark, and the US, outperforming Japan, Germany, and Russia. This significant eight-position jump marks Kazakhstan as the first country in its region to achieve such a high level of digital governance.

item.title: Wild Argali Sheep Spotted Among Livestock in Kyrgyzstan's Leilek District
item.description: A local resident in Kyrgyzstan's Leilek district filmed a rare sight: two wild argali sheep grazing alongside domestic livestock. The footage was sent to the Ministry of Natural Resources, Ecology, and Technical Supervision. According to the ministry, 144 Severtzov's argali were recorded in the Batken region by the end of 2025, highlighting the importance of protecting these animals.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches Online Application for Early Retirement Due to Redundancy
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced an online application system for early retirement for citizens dismissed due to company liquidation or staff reduction. Eligible individuals include men aged 58-60 and women aged 53-55 with the required work experience. The service is free of charge for eligible applicants.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan to Strengthen Inter-Parliamentary Ties
item.description: The Speaker of the Jogorku Kenesh of Kyrgyzstan, Marlen Mamataliev, met with the Chairperson of the Mejlis of Turkmenistan, Dunyagozel Gulmanova, in Turkmenbashi. They discussed enhancing bilateral relations, strengthening inter-parliamentary cooperation, and expanding collaboration in trade, economy, energy, transport, and culture.

item.title: Tajikistan Sees 23% Increase in Tourists from January-September 2026
item.description: Tajikistan hosted 1.73 million foreign citizens in January-September 2026, a 13.6% increase year-on-year. Of these, 1.55 million were classified as tourists, marking a 23% rise. Most visitors, 90.1%, came from CIS countries, with Uzbekistan and Russia being the primary sources.

item.title: Armenian PM threatens resignation over proposed constitutional referendum
item.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan has vowed to resign if a proposed constitutional referendum fails to gain majority support, and will not seek re-election if it succeeds. The new constitution is central to his "Real Armenia" program and could facilitate a peace agreement with Azerbaijan by removing constitutional clauses questioning Azerbaijan's sovereignty over Nagorno-Karabakh.

item.title: Tajikistan's Ministry of Energy Comments on Collapse of Uzbek Power Line Support
item.description: A support tower for the 500 kV high-voltage power line L-503 collapsed in Tajikistan's Zafarabad district due to strong winds. The Ministry of Energy and Water Resources stated this did not affect Tajikistan's power supply as the line is not used by its energy system. The incident caused power outages in parts of Uzbekistan.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets with Head of International Judo Federation
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan met with the head of the International Judo Federation to discuss expanding cooperation in developing the national judo school and training young athletes. The meeting focused on strengthening the partnership between the federation and Uzbekistan's sports institutions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Signs Agreement on Youth Employment and Safe Migration
item.description: Uzbekistan has signed a trilateral memorandum of cooperation aimed at training youth in in-demand professions and foreign languages, and facilitating their employment in the international labor market. The agreement, part of the '2+6' program, will streamline efforts in subsidizing language learning, vocational training, and legal labor migration.

item.title: Pentagon Estimates War with Iran Would Cost the US Over $48 Billion
item.description: A Pentagon assessment suggests that a war with Iran would cost the United States more than $48 billion. The provided text is incomplete, offering no further details on the nature of the conflict or the breakdown of these costs.

item.title: Xi Jinping: China-Russia-US Trilateral Meeting Will Yield Significant Future Results
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping stated that the first trilateral meeting between China, Russia, and the United States in Shenzhen will produce significant future results. He emphasized the need for strengthened cooperation to overcome global challenges, suggesting that shared interests can foster peace and mutual benefit.

item.title: International Court of Justice Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya
item.description: The International Court of Justice has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority. The court ordered safe return and reparations for refugees. This is the first time in the court's 80-year history that it has found a country guilty of genocide, citing systematic destruction and violence.

item.title: Navoiy Region Enterprises to Develop Using German Technologies
item.description: Cooperation is being established in the Navoiy region to enhance the technological capabilities of industrial enterprises, localize component production for the automotive industry, and facilitate market access to Europe. A memorandum signed with the Ministry of Economy and Finance aims to adapt local businesses to European standards and explore innovation institute creation.

item.title: British Library Manuscripts on Display in Tajikistan's Khujand Fortress Museum
item.description: Copies of 18 classical Persian-Tajik literature manuscripts from the British Library are exhibited at the Khujand Fortress Museum in Tajikistan. The exhibition, running until January 2027, marks 35 years of UK-Tajikistan diplomatic ties and 25 years of the British embassy in Dushanbe. It showcases works by Rudaki, Firdawsi, Omar Khayyam, and Kamoli Khujandi.

item.title: Turkmenistan's National Leader Meets with Speaker of Russia's Federation Council
item.description: Turkmenistan's National Leader and Chairman of the Halk Maslahaty, Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow, held a meeting with Valentina Matviyenko, Speaker of the Federation Council of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation. Matviyenko expressed gratitude for the hospitality and affirmed Russia's commitment to developing friendly relations and effective cooperation with Turkmenistan, acknowledging Berdimuhamedow's significant contributions. She also conveyed warm greetings from Russian President Vladimir Putin and recalled his positive visit to Turkmenistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Identify New Priorities for Economic Cooperation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz to discuss boosting economic ties. The meeting, part of the first Uzbek-Turkish High-Level Business Support Council, highlighted strong interest in expanding partnership. Uzbekistan's economy has tripled since 2017, attracting significant foreign investment, with Turkey noted as a key strategic partner.

item.title: Turkmenistan's National Leader Meets with CIS Executive Secretary
item.description: Turkmenistan's National Leader and Chairman of the Halk Maslahaty, Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow, met with Sergey Lebedev, Executive Secretary of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS). Lebedev expressed gratitude for the opportunity and hospitality, highlighting Turkmenistan's significant role in expanding equal and mutually beneficial cooperation within the CIS and implementing its programs. He noted Turkmenistan's continuous development under President Serdar Berdimuhamedow and the opening of opportunities for strengthening cooperation, particularly in economy and transport-logistics.

item.title: Turkmenistan's National Leader Conducts Working Visit to Balkan Region
item.description: Turkmenistan's National Leader and Chairman of the Halk Maslahaty, Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow, undertook a working visit to the Balkan region. He arrived at the international airport in Ashgabat and discussed with officials. Berdimuhamedow noted that the ongoing 61st plenary session of the CIS Parliamentary Assembly in Avaza demonstrates the successful implementation of Turkmenistan's foreign policy based on neutrality and its emphasis on effective foreign partnerships. He also highlighted upcoming events, including a charity event for children in partnership with UNICEF.

item.title: Turkmenistan President Extends Greetings at CIS Parliamentary Assembly Meeting
item.description: Turkmenistan's President Serdar Berdimuhamedow conveyed warm greetings and best wishes at the CIS Parliamentary Assembly Council meeting. The assembly has developed a substantial legislative framework over many years, with economic issues being a primary focus since its inception in 1992. The UN General Assembly adopted a two-year resolution on cooperation between the UN and the CIS.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Silk Sector Exploits Farmers With Forced Labor and Unpaid Work
item.description: A report documents forced cocoon production and exploitative conditions for rural families in Uzbekistan's silk sector. Farmers face pressure to meet quotas, sign blank contracts, and struggle with payment, sometimes receiving nothing. The government promotes silk production for jobs and exports, but producers endure hardship and financial loss.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Expand Cooperation in Geology and Mining
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkey are strengthening their partnership in the geology and mining sectors. Uzbek Minister of Mining and Geology Bobur Islamov held talks with delegations from Turkish companies "ESAN" and "Eksim Holding." Discussions focused on joint projects, attracting foreign investment, and implementing innovative technologies.

item.title: Brazilian Woman Faces Severe Penalties for Drug Smuggling on Bali
item.description: A Brazilian woman was arrested on the Indonesian island of Bali for suspected drug smuggling. Authorities found over 3.6 kg of liquid cocaine hidden in personal hygiene products in her luggage. She faces a potential life sentence.

item.title: Uzbek Riders Secure Top Places in Eurasian League World Cup
item.description: Uzbekistan's equestrian team achieved notable success at the Eurasian League World Cup finals in Astana. Alisherjon Erkinov secured first place in the 125 cm competition, followed by A'zam Tolibboev in second. A rider from Kyrgyzstan took third.

item.title: Afghan UN Envoy Advocates for Women's Rights and Public Participation in Afghanistan's Future
item.description: Afghanistan's UN Representative, Nasir Ahmad Faiq, urged support for citizens' rights, education, and employment for women and girls. He emphasized public participation in shaping the country's future and pledged to convey the Afghan people's voices globally, striving for an independent and peaceful Afghanistan.

item.title: Group Arrested in Karakalpakstan for Allegedly Embezzling 1 Billion Som via Malicious APK Files
item.description: A group has been apprehended in Karakalpakstan on suspicion of embezzling approximately 1 billion Uzbek soums using malicious APK files. Investigators discovered data from 162 bank cards in the suspects' Telegram communications. The stolen funds were reportedly used to purchase expensive phones and fund betting accounts.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Eco-Police Finds Violations in Air Pollution Control at Tashkent Plant
item.description: Uzbekistan's eco-police discovered violations of air pollution control measures at an ООО "R.P." plant in Tashkent. The facility, producing polyethylene granules, failed to implement atmospheric protection measures, conduct emissions monitoring, or install necessary gas cleaning equipment. Air samples showed elevated levels of nitrogen dioxide and dust.
